transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-10
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Owen (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (CTO, Apogee), Rahul (SRE), Maria (Lead ML), Evan (PM)

Summary:
Quick runthrough of Apogee's constraints: heavy traffic spikes, on-prem data residency, and existing API gateway that handles auth and rate-limiting. Goal: determine feasibility of Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private and integration surface (SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway sidecar/proxy).

Topics:
- SDK usage and language support (python/node/java)
- LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters and best-practices
- Gateway/proxy pattern vs direct SDK in service mesh
- Rate limits, quotas and upstream token billing mapping
- Observability hooks (tracing, per-route token counts, logs)
- Security: VPC, KMS, SOC2/audit logs

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intros?
00:06 Lena: yeah lena here, CTO at apogee, i'll kick off - we run a mix of public cloud and colo, and are evaluating options to move some inference workloads off our in-house cluster.
00:18 Maya: great, i'll give a 5 min overview of options then owen will dig into integration.
00:26 Owen: hi all. so at a high level redwood gives three deployment modes - hosted api, dedicated pools, and private vpc/on-prem. from an integration POV for teams like yours we usually see two patterns: gateway/proxy pattern where your gateway calls redwood, or a sidecar/sdk inside your services. both pros/cons.
00:48 Maria: quick q - we use langchain heavy in our pipelines and a bunch of LlamaIndex in search augmentation. how well does redwood play with those? any adapter code?
01:02 Owen: yeah we have example adapters and a small repo we share - langchain's llm wrapper, and a LlamaIndex connector for embeddings and rerank. caveat - some model-specific params might need tuning; LlamaIndex's chunking + kv cache behaviours interact with our batching. we can provide a sample repo that mirrors your pipeline.
01:18 Maria: ok that's helpful. are those examples in both python and node?
01:22 Owen: python first, node examples as well. java is community-driven but we do have sdk endpoints and a simple rest wrapper.
01:31 Rahul: on the gateway side we already have a rate-limiter and API key system. if we point the gateway at redwood, how do we map our quotas and handle bursty traffic?
01:42 Diego: so typical pattern is you keep the gateway as the auth/rate-limit layer. requests are proxied to redwood hosted or private endpoints. for rate-limiting we expose per-API-key token counters and you can configure token budgets / quotas per-key. for burst handling we recommend a small local queue + retry/backoff and using dedicated pools or private to reduce cold fallbacks.
02:05 Lena: if we go Hosted, are there SLAs for throughput? we can't have high variability during our marketing spikes.
02:12 Maya: hosted has soft SLAs; for predictable throughput we recommend Dedicated GPUs where you reserve capacity and get tighter SLOs. Private on-prem gives you total control but with more ops.
02:25 Evan: curious about pricing mapping - we bill customers per API call, but redwood is token-based. how do we reconcile without leaking costs?
02:34 Owen: you can map our token counters into your billing pipeline. many customers use per-route tagging and cost attribution hooks we provide; for gateway proxied requests, route metadata gets sent and shows up in the console per-model, per-route token counts.
02:48 Maria: about observability - can we get traces that correlate our request id through redwood to token counts/latency percentiles?
02:56 Diego: yes. we support distributed tracing headers (traceparent/x-b3) and we emit per-request metrics you can pull or stream to a metrics endpoint. we also have a logs export capable of including token usage and truncated prompts for debugging (with PII strip options).
03:15 Rahul: what's the network path for Private - do we allow customer-managed NICs and route tables? how about HSM/KMS integration?
03:22 Owen: for Private we offer a customer-controlled control plane and can peer into your VPC; on-prem install supports customer-managed NICs. KMS integration for key wrapping and HSM options are supported - we can share the architecture doc.
03:34 Lena: security is major - SOC2 and audit logs, SSO for our engineers, RBAC. can you lock down features per team?
03:42 Maya: yes we have SAML SSO, RBAC roles, audit logs that include user actions and model rollouts. SOC2 attestation and the security pack will be in the doc set i send.
03:49 Evan: back to integration: we have a service mesh (istio) - would you recommend sidecar SDKs or gateway pattern?
03:57 Owen: with istio it's often simpler to keep the gateway as the single egress point to Redwood and use a lightweight SDK in the gateway layer that handles batching and cache. Sidecar per-service gives lower latencies but more management overhead. also consider prefix/KV caching at the gateway to reduce token costs.
04:20 Maria: KV cache - explain how that works with long conversational contexts and LlamaIndex persistent indices.
04:27 Diego: KV cache stores autoregressive KV cache across requests for the same session to avoid re-sending context. for LlamaIndex we recommend storing embeddings and index metadata in your vector DB and using redwood for generation only; cache helps when you have session affinity. however watch memory footprint and eviction policies.
04:47 Lena: any known gotchas with quantized models or GPU variants? we run some inference on INT8 at the edge and worry about quality regressions.
04:55 Owen: quantization needs validation - the runtime picks kernels based on model/sequence profile; some customers run A/B tests with generation evals. we can help with a small eval harness to compare fp16 vs int8 quality.
05:10 Rahul: latency targets - we need p95 under 350ms for short completions. what's realistic?
05:18 Diego: on dedicated pools with optimized batching and short sequences, p95 under 200-300ms is common; hosted can vary, so if p95 is critical i'd lean Dedicated or Private colocated.
05:31 Evan: how do rollouts work if we pin model versions and then want a canary?
05:36 Owen: console supports canary rollouts and traffic splits per model/version; automatic fallback to a cheaper model if latency spikes is configurable.
05:47 Maria: do you have examples for LangChain chains that do rerank followed by generate?
05:52 Owen: yes, our langchain examples show a two-stage pattern - embedding + rerank (LlamaIndex/FAISS) then generation; there are notes on batching and timeouts.
06:05 Lena: on ops - if we want to keep gateway auth internal, can we run a proxy that terminates TLS and mTLS to redwood?
06:13 Diego: absolutely. mutual TLS is supported and you can run a gateway sidecar that mTLS to redwood endpoints. many customers add a proxy to perform header enrichment and auth.
06:24 Rahul: curious about rate-limits - suppose we set 100 rps but tokens per request vary, do you do token-based throttling or requests?
06:33 Owen: both. we provide per-second request limits and token throughput budgets. for stability we recommend token budgets because long prompts otherwise eat capacity. gateway can enforce both: request concurrency plus token ceilings.
06:47 Evan: what's the onboarding timeline if we want dedicated? we have a Q2 target to run live for selected flows.
06:54 Maya: typical time to dedicated SLA from contract is 4-8 weeks depending on capacity and networking. private can take longer for on-prem installs. for a pilot we can do hosted + dedicated eval in 2-3 weeks (sandbox + basic benchmarks).
07:08 Maria: any recommended benchmarking scripts we can run?
07:12 Owen: yes we'll share a small harness - sample workloads, sequence distributions, latency/throughput collectors, and a cost estimator.
07:20 Lena: ok let's talk about immediate actions - we want Redwood to run a short smoke test against our gateway with a few sample endpoints to measure end-to-end latency.
07:27 Maya: we can do that. we'll need a sample token and an IP allowlist or vpn. Diego will prepare instructions.
07:33 Diego: i'll send a checklist for firewall rules and an example curl-based test, plus the langchain repo.
07:38 Evan: and we'll send our 7-day traffic csv and current gateway rate-limit config.
07:42 Maya: perfect. any open questions from the team?
07:45 Maria: small one - do you expose per-prompt embedding logs for privacy reasons?
07:50 Owen: we can redact or not store prompt text; by default we store truncated prompts for debugging but customers can opt out and retain only token counts/metrics.
07:59 Lena: that's fine. last, can you include a sketch for a hybrid approach — gateway + light sdk in critical services?
08:06 Diego: yes, i will include a diagram and pros/cons.
08:12 Maya: recap of next steps: send security pack + private deploy checklist, share langchain/llamaindex example repo, Owen to produce benchmarking harness, Apogee to share traffic + gateway config, schedule infra deep-dive next week.
08:25 Lena: thanks everyone — this was useful.
08:28 Maya: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
